scope: Original-source check of tortoise feeding records. Not a safety verdict; A-D grades are unchanged.
rules: A candidate is a lead, not a feeding record.
A feeding record is verified only from the full text of the original; a title or abstract never confirms it.
Recommendations in care sheets and citations of other studies are not feeding records.
Genus-level names never become species records; names with unresolved homonyms are not linked.
feeding_pending = verified full-text feeding record linked unambiguously to a catalog entry with no A-D grade.
Feeding details are filled only when the original states them; otherwise null (not reported).

records.citation: El Mouden, E. H., Slimani, T., Ben Kaddour, K., Lagarde, F., Ouhammou, A. & Bonnet, X. (2006) Testudo graeca graeca feeding ecology in an arid and overgrazed zone in Morocco. J. Arid Environ. 64:422-435
records.original_summary: The abstract states that faecal analysis of T. g. graeca in the central Jbilets found five main plant species (Leontodon saxatilis, Malva parviflora, Astragalus cruciatus, Medicago hispida, Lotus arenarius) making up 70% of identified material and highly preferred. No page, table, plant part or per-species share is given, so no record is confirmed from the full text (QA-FR-001).

Ruscus aculeatus L.
records.original_opened: BioOne abstract (2026-10-17); author-uploaded full text on ResearchGate reviewed by the owner (2026-10-19, data/ruscus_primary_fulltext_review_20261019.json). Not reopened by this pipeline: publisher copy subscriber-only, Unpaywall/OpenAlex closed, ResearchGate and IRIS/CRIS return 403
records.citation: Del Vecchio, S., Burke, R. L., Rugiero, L., Capula, M. & Luiselli, L. (2011) Seasonal changes in the diet of Testudo hermanni hermanni in central Italy. Herpetologica 67(3):236-249
records.original_locator: Table 1, p. 240 and Table 2, p. 241 (Ruscus aculeatus: fruits, seeds; faecal remains); Discussion, p. 245 (leaves eaten in autumn); abstract (flowers and unripe fruit in autumn)
records.original_summary: Faecal tables list Ruscus aculeatus fruits and seeds (Table 1 p. 240; Table 2 p. 241: spring 1/28, autumn 21/21). The Discussion (p. 245) states the tortoises also ate the leaves in autumn; leaves are not in the tables. The abstract mentions flowers and unripe fruit in autumn. Not yet a full-text extract (site and period locators missing), so not counted as a confirmed feeding record (see QA-FR-002).
